name: Nuvama Wealth Management Ltd
title: Nuvama Wealth Management Ltd - 543988 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Record Q1 FY27 quarter: revenue INR909 crore (+18%) and PAT ~INR300 crore, with cost-to-income near 55% and FY guidance held; capital-cycle signals are not the story here, growth and flows are.

summary.headline: Nuvama Q1 FY27 record quarter: revenue INR909 crores (+18% YoY) and operating PAT INR306 crores (+16% YoY), with client assets at INR5.36 lakh crores.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly profit above INR300 crores and revenue of INR909 crores, with ROE near 30%. Client assets crossed INR5 lakh crores, and MPIS plus ARR assets together crossed INR1 lakh crores. Asset services grew about 34% YoY, but management warned that growth will moderate, and part of the fixed income windfall (INR15-20 crores) may not repeat. Cost-to-income was about 55%, and management guided to a full-year opex growth of 15-16% plus an unspecified new office lease charge.

segments.name: Nuvama Wealth (MPIS)
segments.commentary: MPIS revenue up ~20% YoY; assets ~INR42,500-43,000 crores (+32% YoY); Tier 2+ now more than 35% of contribution. Wealth cost-to-income down 160 bps; advisory yield framed at 80-90 bps for ARR.

segments.name: Nuvama Private (ARR)
segments.commentary: ARR assets ~INR58,000 crores (+20-21%); ARR net flows ~INR1,000 crores in Q1 after weeding out low-yield legacy mandates. FY target remains 20-22% growth of opening assets. Private cost-to-income ~70%, guided lower for FY27 vs 66% last year.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.commentary: PRIME commercial real estate fund closed at INR4,000 crores (target INR3,000 crores), ~40% deployed. Second CRE fund targeted at INR4,000-5,000 crores by end Q3. Crossover 4 PE fund at INR300-350 crores raised vs INR700-1,000 crores target. Quarterly cost INR30-33 crores, peaking at INR35-36 crores; FY27 cumulative loss INR35-40 crores.

segments.name: Asset Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR260 crores, +34% YoY, with ~20% QoQ growth. Management cautioned against repeating this pace; FY revenue growth guided at 20-25%.

segments.name: Capital Markets (IE + IB)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR180 crores, flat YoY. Fixed income in IB was strong after the 7 June G-Sec tax change; ECM weak with Q1 IPO fundraise down ~60-65%. Full-year cost-to-income guided at 36-40% for this segment.

segments.name: Offshore (Dubai, Singapore)
segments.commentary: Dubai broke even; Singapore expected to break even by end of FY27. Offshore expected to contribute 5-7% of revenue this year.

guidance_outlook: Full-year opex growth 15-16%: about two-thirds inflation and business-linked, one-third new initiatives; new office lease charge (Ind AS 116) to be added on top, not yet finalised.
Full-year consolidated cost-to-income around 55%, with quarterly swings of about +/-1%.
Asset services FY revenue growth of 20-25%, with quarter-on-quarter moderation expected.
Private ARR flow target of 20-22% of opening assets for FY27; private cost-to-income FY27 below FY26 (~66%) and medium-term 60-62% wealth target retained over three years.
Indicative FY27 net flows: wealth and private INR10,000-12,000 crores each; AMC INR3,500-5,500 crores.
Private transactional income FY27 expected at INR350-360 crores vs ~INR300-305 crores in FY26; 20% of transactional income is opportunistic.
Asset management breakeven expected to start after FY27, with revenue inflection from Q4 as new products launch.
Lending cost of debt: blended 40-50 bps could be added to the current ~3.7-3.8% period-end lending margin.
Management expects equity mix in managed products to rise from 30-35% over the next two quarters.
capex_capacity: Net RM additions: ~11% (about 15 net) over last 12 months, 6-8 in Q1; target 15-16% a year if markets allow.
Physical offices in top 70-80 locations; presence in 65-70 cities directly and 400-450 pin codes via external wealth managers.
Second CRE fund (INR4,000-5,000 crores) targeted by end Q3 FY27; long-term REIT platform being considered within 24 months.
Private credit fund: team build-out 2-2.5 months; first fund launch around mid-to-end Q3.
RTA and trustee offering rollout expected in about one more quarter; targeted at PMS and AIF clients only.
Office lease renewal under evaluation; costs to be disclosed at quarterly results.
demand_pricing: Private segment RM competition has intensified; management says the company is still adding RMs.
Management says private yields will stay in an 80-90 bps range; can exceed 1% when a blockbuster AIF II/III product is in a quarter. Advisory impact expected to show next year.
Advisory book (ARR) is ~INR13,000 crores of ~INR58,500 crores total; advisory share growing.
Wealth retention fell from ~90 bps to 85 bps, attributed to insurance seasonality and total-yield accounting effects of market mark-to-market.
Venture debt fund fees were waived for three quarters and restarted in Q1, lifting AMC yields.
Public markets had redemptions in absolute return and long-short funds, as clients shift to SIF structures; SIF licence pending.
Q1 IPOs: 8 (vs 15 in Q4 and 14-15 a year ago); IPO fundraise down ~60-65% YoY and QoQ. Pipeline reported to be building.
Fixed income IB activity was strong because of the 7 June G-Sec tax exemption; some INR10-20 crores of income may not recur.
Management flagged STT, intraday financing and bank guarantee collateral rules on derivatives as a monitorable, but does not expect a significant impact.

financial_highlights.value: ~INR1,000 crores net (INR1,800 crores in the prior-year framing used on call)
financial_highlights.change: Soft on net basis due to mandate cleanup

qa_highlights.question: Private segment cost-to-income is about 70%; when will it trend toward the 60-62% wealth target, and what RM additions are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is not a fair base: Q1 FY26 was 69% and Q1 FY27 is 70% with profit up about 22%, as variable pay tracks revenue. FY26 was about 66% and FY27 should be lower. RM adds target 15-16% a year if markets allow; net adds were about 11% (15 RMs) in the last 12 months and 6 in Q1. The 60-62% medium-term target holds over three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did wealth retention fall from about 90 bps to 85 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance seasonality (higher Q4 and Q1 income on a lower denominator) and total-yield accounting, where mark-to-market gains lower reported yield when brokerage does not rise in step.

qa_highlights.question: Will the AMC/venture debt yield uplift last?
qa_highlights.answer: Venture debt fees were waived for three quarters and resumed in Q1, which is the main driver. Management said it will sustain unless the fee is waived again.

qa_highlights.question: Asset services: will growth be yield-driven rather than flow-driven, and what is the FY cost-to-income for capital markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Flows continue, but some collateral may shift from cash to G-Secs, so yield adjusts. Capital markets full-year cost-to-income is guided at 36-40%, with ECM and part of IE under pressure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the lending margin outlook and cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Current period-end lending margin is about 3.7-3.8%. Blended cost of debt can add 40-50 bps from current levels, since hedging on the MLD book (about 25% of borrowings) makes the saving swing by quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How should the ESOP/ESAR cost and dilution be viewed over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Company is moving to stock appreciation rights (ESARs) subject to shareholder approval. Management cited 7.5% pool and about 3% dilution at 20% annual price growth. Cost is about INR300-400 crores over five years, noncash, and roughly INR150 crores net after tax benefits.

qa_highlights.question: Is the advisory shift likely to pull private ARR yields lower, and how big is the advisory book?
qa_highlights.answer: Advisory book is about INR13,000 crores of about INR58,500 crores ARR. Private yields should stay in an 80-90 bps range, and can exceed 1% in a quarter with a blockbuster AIF product. Management said advisory's yield impact should show next year.

risks_watch: Asset services growth moderation: management guided against repeating the ~20% QoQ pace, with FY revenue growth of 20-25%, and collateral shifting from cash to G-Secs could change yield.
Fixed income windfall: INR10-20 crores of IB fixed income income may not recur; capital markets revenue is flat at ~INR180 crores with ECM weak (Q1 IPO fundraise down ~60-65%).
Opex and new office lease: FY opex growth 15-16% plus an unquantified Ind AS 116 upfront lease charge; the cost will be disclosed with quarterly results.

Asset management losses: quarterly cost of INR30-33 crores peaking at INR35-36 crores; FY27 cumulative loss INR35-40 crores; crossover 4 PE fund at INR300-350 crores vs INR700-1,000 crores target; public markets redemptions as clients shift to SIF (licence pending).
Derivatives regulation (STT, intraday financing, bank guarantee collateral) flagged as monitorable; management does not expect a significant impact. Private RM competition has intensified.
key_quotes: Our quarterly revenues crossed INR900 crores, and our quarterly PAT crossed INR300 crores, an all -time high for us.
There will be some amount of moderation as new client acquisition has happened and a lot of collateral is right now sitting in cash, which will get converted between cash and G-Secs.
So this year, we will end up at a cumulative loss of around INR35 crores to INR40 crores.
Our target for the full year still remains at 20 -22% of the opening assets.
summary.management_tone: Confident on franchise scale, record profit and the ARR and MPIS milestones, but cautious on forward momentum: management repeatedly warned that asset services and fixed-income gains will moderate and that Q1 should not be used as a base for private cost-to-income. It was candid on the drag from asset management start-ups and on the unquantified lease charge, and it avoided giving segment-level capital markets PBT.

adds.what: PRIME CRE fund closed at INR4,000 crores (AUM fund raise, not physical capacity)
Second CRE fund targeted at INR4,000-5,000 crores
Private credit fund first launch around mid-to-end Q3
RTA and trustee offering rollout for PMS and AIF clients
Net RM additions target 15-16% a year (6-8 in Q1)

growth.why: Management guides to FY27 asset services revenue growth of 20-25%, ARR flow target of 20-22% of opening assets, and indicative net flows of INR10,000-12,000 crores each for wealth and private, but warns that growth will moderate and the INR15-20 crore fixed income windfall may not recur; no consolidated revenue growth guide is given and capital markets is flat YoY.
